title: Scale the portions, not the pan
hook: A four-portion recipe uses 300g. How much corresponds to six portions?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

misconception: The same ingredient quantity serves more people without changing portion size.
objective: Scale a recipe quantity while preserving quantity per portion.

claims.text: The original rate is 75g per portion. Multiply that rate by the new portion count to keep the same amount per person. This demonstrates proportional quantity arithmetic, not cooking or nutritional advice.

claims.text: A quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. How many grams keep the same amount per portion for two portions? Correct: 150g. The rate is 75g per portion; two portions × 75g = 150g. This is proportional quantity arithmetic only.
claims.source: Quantity-only arithmetic: 300g ÷ 4 portions = 75g/portion; 75g/portion × 2 portions = 150g (the current recall). recall.question: A quantity-only recipe uses 300g for four equal portions. How many grams keep the same amount per portion for two portions?
recall.why: The rate is 75g per portion; two portions × 75g = 150g. This is proportional quantity arithmetic only.
